claim: NFATc2 was significantly overexpressed in human primary NSCLC compared to normal lung.
source: By analyzing transcripts expression, we observed NFATc2 was significantly overexpressed in human primary NSCLC compared to normal lung (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by qPCR analysis shown in Figure 1A with p=0.0003 by Wilcoxon test.

claim: High level activated NFATc2 expression with intense and widespread nuclear staining were detected in 41 of 102 (40.2%) excised primary NSCLC.
source: Using IHC, high level activated NFATc2 expression with intense and widespread nuclear staining were detected in 41 of 102 (40.2%) excised primary NSCLC, while 61 (59.8%) showed low expression with weak nuclear and/or cytoplasmic staining in isolated or small clusters of tumor cells (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: Based on immunohistochemical analysis of 102 NSCLC samples with quantitative scoring.

claim: In normal lung epithelium, NFATc2 was expressed in the bronchiolar stem cell compartment of basal reserve cells while differentiated bronchiolar cells or alveolar pneumocytes were negative.
source: In normal lung epithelium, NFATc2 was expressed in the bronchiolar stem cell compartment of basal reserve cells while differentiated bronchiolar cells or alveolar pneumocytes were negative (Figure 1D).
evidence: Demonstrated by IHC staining pattern in normal bronchial epithelium shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Tumors with high level NFATc2 expression had significantly shorter recurrence-free survival (RFS) and cancer-specific overall survival (OS).
source: Using log rank test and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, we showed tumors with high level NFATc2 expression had significantly shorter recurrence-free survival (RFS) and cancer-specific overall survival (OS) (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: Demonstrated by Kaplan-Meier survival curves with log-rank test showing p=0.008 for RFS and p=0.003 for OS.

claim: High NFATc2 expression significantly predicted poor tumor differentiation, advanced tumor stage and TNM stage.
source: High NFATc2 expression significantly predicted poor tumor differentiation, advanced tumor stage and TNM stage (Table 1A).
evidence: Supported by chi-square test analysis showing p=0.019 for differentiation, p=0.001 for tumor stage, and p=0.014 for TNM stage.

claim: High NFATc2, late pathological stage, age and smoking history were independent prognostic indicators for shorter OS.
source: Multivariate Cox regression analysis further showed high NFATc2, late pathological stage, age and smoking history were independent prognostic indicators for shorter OS, while high NFATc2 and advanced pathological stage were predictive for shorter RFS (Table 1B, C).
evidence: Demonstrated by multivariate Cox regression analysis with p=0.002 for NFATc2, p=0.012 for TNM stage, p=0.01 for age, and p=0.009 for smoking history.

claim: High NFATc2 and advanced pathological stage were predictive for shorter RFS.
source: Multivariate Cox regression analysis further showed high NFATc2, late pathological stage, age and smoking history were independent prognostic indicators for shorter OS, while high NFATc2 and advanced pathological stage were predictive for shorter RFS (Table 1B, C).
evidence: Demonstrated by multivariate Cox regression analysis with p=0.037 for NFATc2 and p=0.001 for TNM stage.

claim: TIC showed higher NFATc2 expression by Western blot compared to non-TIC growing in monolayers.
source: TIC showed higher NFATc2 expression by Western blot (Figure 2A), while transcripts of NFATc2 and its target FASL were also significantly upregulated (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot analysis comparing tumorspheres to monolayer cultures in 4 lung AD cell lines.

claim: Transcripts of NFATc2 and its target FASL were significantly upregulated in TIC compared to non-TIC.
source: TIC showed higher NFATc2 expression by Western blot (Figure 2A), while transcripts of NFATc2 and its target FASL were also significantly upregulated (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis showing significant upregulation in tumorspheres versus monolayers.

claim: TIC isolated from H1299 and A549 cells showed significantly higher NFAT activities in spheres.
source: Luciferase reporter assays also showed significantly higher NFAT activities in spheres isolated from H1299 and A549 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated by NFAT luciferase reporter assays comparing spheres to monolayers.

claim: TIC selected by the lung TIC markers ALDH+/CD44+ showed higher NFATc2 expression than the ALDH-/CD44- non-TIC counterpart.
source: Furthermore, TIC selected by the lung TIC markers ALDH+/CD44+ from HCC827 and the patient-derived lung cancer cell lines, HKUCL2 and HKUCL4, showed higher NFATc2 expression than the ALDH-/CD44- non-TIC counterpart (Figure 2B)(Liu et al., 2013a).
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot analysis of FACS-sorted ALDH+/CD44+ versus ALDH-/CD44- populations, with citation to prior work.

claim: Using CD166high for TIC isolation from HCC827, NFATc2 was upregulated compared to CD166low cells.
source: Using another lung TIC marker, CD166high, for TIC isolation from HCC827, NFATc2 was also shown to be upregulated (Figure 2C) (Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot comparing CD166high to CD166low populations, with citation to prior work on CD166 as a TIC marker.

claim: NFATc2 knockdown did not significantly affect the proliferation and cell cycle distribution of HCC827 cells.
source: As shown by BrdU proliferation assay and cell cycle assay, NFATc2 knockdown did not significantly affect the proliferation and cell cycle distribution of HCC827 cells (Figure 2E and F, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Demonstrated by BrdU assay and flow cytometry cell cycle analysis showing no significant differences.

claim: Abrogation of NFATc2 significantly reduced 60–70% of tumorspheres in all the cell models and inhibited tumorspheres renewability for 2 consecutive generations.
source: However, abrogation of NFATc2 significantly reduced 60–70% of tumorspheres in all the cell models and inhibited tumorspheres renewability for 2 consecutive generations (Figure 2G–I), while overexpression significantly augmented tumorspheres in both A549 and H1299 (Figure 2J–K).
evidence: Demonstrated by tumorsphere formation and serial passage assays in multiple cell lines with NFATc2 knockdown or knockout.

claim: NFATc2 overexpression significantly augmented tumorspheres in both A549 and H1299.
source: However, abrogation of NFATc2 significantly reduced 60–70% of tumorspheres in all the cell models and inhibited tumorspheres renewability for 2 consecutive generations (Figure 2G–I), while overexpression significantly augmented tumorspheres in both A549 and H1299 (Figure 2J–K).
evidence: Demonstrated by tumorsphere formation and serial passage assays showing increased sphere numbers with NFATc2 overexpression.

claim: Treatment with both CSA and FK506 significantly inhibited sphere formation of HCC827 cells.
source: Treatment with both CSA and FK506 significantly inhibited sphere formation of HCC827 cells (Figure 2L).
evidence: Demonstrated by tumorsphere formation assay with calcineurin inhibitors CSA (1 µM) and FK506 (5 µM).

claim: Silencing NFATc2 significantly reduced the migration and invasion ability of both HCC827 and PDCL#24 cells.
source: Transwell assays for cell motility showed silencing NFATc2 significantly reduced the migration and invasion ability of both HCC827 and PDCL#24 cells (Figure 2M–N), while the opposite effects were rendered by NFATc2 overexpression in A549 and H1299 cells (Figure 2O–P).
evidence: Demonstrated by transwell migration and invasion assays with NFATc2 knockdown.

claim: NFATc2 overexpression enhanced migration and invasion in A549 and H1299 cells.
source: Transwell assays for cell motility showed silencing NFATc2 significantly reduced the migration and invasion ability of both HCC827 and PDCL#24 cells (Figure 2M–N), while the opposite effects were rendered by NFATc2 overexpression in A549 and H1299 cells (Figure 2O–P).
evidence: Demonstrated by transwell migration and invasion assays with NFATc2 overexpression.

claim: NFATc2 knockdown significantly reduced tumor sizes and retarded growth rates of HCC827 and PDCL#24 xenografts.
source: Subcutaneous xenograft models showed NFATc2 knockdown significantly reduced tumor sizes and retarded growth rates of HCC827 and PDCL#24, respectively (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: Demonstrated by subcutaneous xenograft experiments with tumor volume measurements over time (p<0.0001 by two-way ANOVA).

claim: NFATc2 expression was detected in xenografts established from HCC827 and PDCL#24 knockdown cells, indicating successful tumorigenesis preferentially involved cells that had selected away from NFATc2 knockdown.
source: Using IHC, NFATc2 expression was detected in xenografts established from HCC827 and PDCL#24 knockdown cells (Figure 3C), indicating successful tumorigenesis preferentially involved cells that had selected away from NFATc2 knockdown.
evidence: Demonstrated by IHC analysis of xenograft tumors showing NFATc2 expression despite knockdown, suggesting selection pressure.

claim: NFATc2 overexpression in A549 significantly augmented tumor growth in vivo.
source: In contrast, NFATc2 overexpression in A549 significantly augmented tumor growth (Figure 3D).
evidence: Demonstrated by subcutaneous xenograft experiments showing increased tumor volumes (p<0.0001 by two-way ANOVA).

claim: NFATc2 knockdown led to significantly reduced xenograft incidence and TIC frequency of HCC827.
source: NFATc2 knockdown led to significantly reduced xenograft incidence and TIC frequency of HCC827 (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by limiting dilution assay showing reduced TIC frequency from 1/455 to 1/1448 and 1/11039 with p=0.029 and p=0.0001.

claim: NFATc2 overexpression increased TIC frequency in A549 cells.
source: Reciprocal effects were observed with NFATc2-overexpression, (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated by limiting dilution assay showing increased TIC frequency from 1/1280 to 1/226 with p=0.0026.

claim: NFATc2 inhibition sensitized PDCL#24 cells to cisplatin with statistically significant reduction of IC50.
source: Upon NFATc2 inhibition, sensitization to cisplatin with statistically significant reduction of IC50 was observed compared to control cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: Demonstrated by MTT assay showing IC50 reduction from 9.9±1.1µM to 4.2±0.6µM and 3.8±0.13µM with NFATc2 knockdown.

claim: NFATc2 knockout as well as CSA and FK506 treatment sensitized HCC827 to cisplatin with reduction of IC50.
source: Similarly, NFATc2 knockout as well as CSA and FK506 treatment also sensitized HCC827 to cisplatin with reduction of IC50 (p<0.01) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, Figure 4B).
evidence: Demonstrated by MTT assays showing IC50 reduction with NFATc2 knockout and calcineurin inhibitors.

claim: Overexpressing NFATc2 in A549 increased cisplatin resistance with significantly elevated IC50.
source: In contrast, overexpressing NFATc2 in A549 increased cisplatin resistance with significantly elevated IC50 (p<0.01) (Figure 4C).
evidence: Demonstrated by MTT assay showing IC50 increase from 12.5±0.7µM to 23.4±0.56µM with NFATc2 overexpression.

claim: In vivo, mice bearing PDCL#24 xenografts treated with cisplatin alone showed 1.68 fold tumor shrinkage compared with vehicle control, while with additional stable NFATc2 knockdown, tumor shrinkage was enhanced to 3.15 and 2.2 fold relative to respective vehicle controls.
source: In vivo, mice bearing PDCL#24 xenografts treated with cisplatin alone showed 1.68 fold tumor shrinkage compared with vehicle control. With additional stable NFATc2 knockdown, tumor shrinkage was enhanced to 3.15 and 2.2 fold relative to respective vehicle controls (p<0.01) (Figure 4D), while tumor growth rate was also retarded (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated by in vivo xenograft experiments with cisplatin treatment (4 mg/kg every three days) and tumor volume measurements.

claim: NFATc2 knockdown significantly increased paclitaxel sensitivity of HCC827 cells.
source: Besides cisplatin, NFATc2 knockdown significantly increased paclitaxel sensitivity of HCC827 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Demonstrated by MTT assay showing IC50 reduction from 21.5±2.64 M to 8.6±1.64nM and 11.3±1.91nM.

claim: A549 cells induced for cisplatin resistance (A549 CR) showed elevated IC50 with NFATc2 upregulation compared to parental A549 cells.
source: A549 cells induced for cisplatin resistance by chronic progressive drug exposure (A549 CR) showed elevated IC50 with NFATc2 upregulation compared to parental A549 cells (Figure 4E–F).
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot showing NFATc2 upregulation and MTT assay showing IC50 increase from 9.4±2.03µM to 18.8±2.83µM.

claim: With NFATc2 suppression, A549 CR was re-sensitized with return of IC50 to around the pre-induction level.
source: With NFATc2 suppression, A549 CR was re-sensitized with return of IC50 to around the pre-induction level (p<0.01) (Figure 4F).
evidence: Demonstrated by MTT assay showing IC50 reduction from 18.8±2.83µM to 12.7±1.4µM and 9.9±0.65µM with NFATc2 knockdown.

claim: Induction of H1299 for paclitaxel resistance caused NFATc2 upregulation.
source: In line with this observation, induction of H1299 for paclitaxel resistance also caused NFATc2 upregulation (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot comparing H1299 parental and paclitaxel resistant (TR) cells.

claim: NFATc2 knockdown or knockout led to significantly reduced IC50 for the TKI gefitinib in HCC827 cells.
source: To investigate whether NFATc2 contributes to targeted therapy resistance, NFATc2 was stably inhibited by shRNA knockdown or CRISPR knockout. This led to significantly reduced IC50 for the TKI gefitinib (Figure 4G,H).
evidence: Demonstrated by MTT assays showing IC50 reduction from 20.6±2.22nM to 11.8±1.58nM and 10.9±0.28nM with knockdown, and from 17.5±2.6nM to 10.5±0.2nM with knockout.

claim: Co-treatment with either CSA or FK506 significantly sensitized HCC827 cells to gefitinib.
source: Similarly, co-treatment with either CSA or FK506, respectively, significantly sensitized HCC827 cells to gefitinib (Figure 4I).
evidence: Demonstrated by MTT assay showing IC50 reduction from 21.8±3.85nM to 5.1±1.2nM with CSA and 8.1±3.2nM with FK506.

claim: In vivo, both groups of NFATc2 knockdown mice showed higher folds of tumor shrinkage (3.57 fold, 4.73 fold, respectively) after 2 weeks of gefitinib treatment compared to scramble control (3.38 fold).
source: In vivo, although both groups of NFATc2 knockdown mice showed higher folds of tumor shrinkage (3.57 fold, 4.73 fold, respectively) after 2 weeks of gefitinib treatment compared to scramble control (3.38 fold) (Figure 4J), the added effects of NFATc2 inhibition were very modest and the effects on the growth curve was not clear-cut (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Demonstrated by in vivo xenograft experiments with gefitinib treatment (25 mg/kg/day by oral gavage) and tumor volume measurements.

claim: In mice with NFATc2 knockdown after short term gefitinib treatment, tumor regrowth was observed in only 3 and 2 mice of the sh-NFATc2-A and sh-NFATc2-B groups, respectively, while all mice in the control group showed tumor regrowth.
source: In mice with NFATc2 knockdown, tumor regrowth was observed in only 3 and 2 mice of the sh-NFATc2-A and sh-NFATc2-B groups, respectively. In contrast, all mice in the control group showed tumor regrowth.
evidence: Demonstrated by in vivo xenograft experiments with short term gefitinib treatment (5 consecutive days) followed by tumor regrowth monitoring.

claim: The NFATc2-inhibited xenografts showed more effective tumor inhibition (5.44 fold, 39.73 fold, respectively) compared to the control group (3.54 fold) after short term gefitinib treatment.
source: The NFATc2-inhibited xenografts showed more effective tumor inhibition (5.44 fold, 39.73 fold, respectively) compared to the control group (3.54 fold) (p<0.01) and differences in tumor volumes on the growth curve were statistically significant (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B–C).
evidence: Demonstrated by in vivo xenograft experiments with tumor volume measurements showing statistically significant differences.

claim: In HCC827 induced for gefitinib resistance (HCC827 GR), NFATc2 was upregulated and NFAT promoter activities were increased compared to parental cells.
source: In HCC827 induced for gefitinib resistance (HCC827 GR), NFATc2 was upregulated and NFAT promoter activities were increased compared to parental cells (Figure 4K–L).
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot and NFAT luciferase reporter assay comparing HCC827 GR to parental cells.

claim: Upon CSA inhibition or sh-NFATc2 knockdown in HCC827 GR, re-sensitization to gefitinib with significantly reduced IC50 resulted.
source: Upon CSA inhibition or sh-NFATc2 knockdown, respectively, re-sensitization to gefitinib with significantly reduced IC50 resulted (Figure 4M).
evidence: Demonstrated by MTT assay showing IC50 reduction from 27.87±1.43µM to 16.54±0.95µM with CSA, 14.7±1.17µM and 12.5±1.97µM with NFATc2 knockdown.

claim: Transcripts of the major stemness factors SOX2, OCT4 and NANOG were significantly elevated in tumorspheres compared to monolayers in 4 lung AD cell lines.
source: Indeed, analysis of 4 lung AD cell lines showed transcripts of the major stemness factors SOX2, OCT4 and NANOG were significantly elevated in tumorspheres compared to monolayers (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis of tumorspheres versus monolayers in H1299, HCC827, HKULC4, and A549 cells.

claim: Genetic inhibition of NFATc2 in HCC827 and PDCL#24 led to consistent SOX2 repression with the highest magnitude of change compared to the other 2 factors (OCT4 and NANOG).
source: Genetic inhibition of NFATc2 in HCC827 and PDCL#24 led to consistent SOX2 repression with the highest magnitude of change compared to the other 2 factors (p<0.01) (Figure 5A–B), while all 3 were significantly upregulated on NFATc2 ectopic expression (Figure 5C–D).
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis showing SOX2 had the most consistent and largest magnitude of change with NFATc2 knockdown.

claim: All 3 pluripotency factors (SOX2, OCT4, NANOG) were significantly upregulated on NFATc2 ectopic expression.
source: Genetic inhibition of NFATc2 in HCC827 and PDCL#24 led to consistent SOX2 repression with the highest magnitude of change compared to the other 2 factors (p<0.01) (Figure 5A–B), while all 3 were significantly upregulated on NFATc2 ectopic expression (Figure 5C–D).
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis in A549 and H1299 cells with NFATc2 overexpression.

claim: Corresponding changes in pluripotency factors were shown at the protein level with NFATc2 manipulation.
source: Corresponding changes were shown at the protein level (Figure 5E).
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot analysis showing SOX2 protein changes with NFATc2 knockdown, knockout, or overexpression.

claim: Inhibition of calcineurin activity by CSA or FK506 consistently down-regulated SOX2 expression in both HCC827 and PDCL#24 cells.
source: Further, inhibition of calcineurin activity either by inhibitors (Figure 5F–G), or by siRNA transient knockdown of one of its subunits PPP3R1 (Figure 5H–I) consistently down-regulated SOX2 expression in both HCC827 and PDCL#24 cells.
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis showing SOX2 downregulation with CSA or FK506 treatment.

claim: siRNA transient knockdown of calcineurin subunit PPP3R1 consistently down-regulated SOX2 expression in both HCC827 and PDCL#24 cells.
source: Further, inhibition of calcineurin activity either by inhibitors (Figure 5F–G), or by siRNA transient knockdown of one of its subunits PPP3R1 (Figure 5H–I) consistently down-regulated SOX2 expression in both HCC827 and PDCL#24 cells.
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis showing SOX2 downregulation with PPP3R1 knockdown.

claim: NFATc1 transient knockdown by siRNA in HCC827 and PDCL#24 cells did not result in consistently reduced SOX2 expression.
source: On the other hand, NFATc1 has been reported to be a transcriptional regulator of SOX2 in pancreatic cancer (Singh et al., 2015). To study whether it is also involved in regulating SOX2, expression in lung AD, NFATc1 was transiently knocked down by siRNA in HCC827 and PDCL#24 cells, which did not result in consistently reduced SOX2 expression (Figure 5J–K), indicating NFATc2, rather than NFATc1, was involved in the regulation of SOX2 expression in lung AD.
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis showing inconsistent SOX2 changes with NFATc1 knockdown, with citation to prior work on NFATc1 in pancreatic cancer.

claim: NFATc2, rather than NFATc1, was involved in the regulation of SOX2 expression in lung AD.
source: On the other hand, NFATc1 has been reported to be a transcriptional regulator of SOX2 in pancreatic cancer (Singh et al., 2015). To study whether it is also involved in regulating SOX2, expression in lung AD, NFATc1 was transiently knocked down by siRNA in HCC827 and PDCL#24 cells, which did not result in consistently reduced SOX2 expression (Figure 5J–K), indicating NFATc2, rather than NFATc1, was involved in the regulation of SOX2 expression in lung AD.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of consistent SOX2 changes with NFATc1 knockdown compared to consistent changes with NFATc2 manipulation.

claim: Four regions encompassing multiple conserved NFAT binding sequences were identified spanning 5 kb up- and downstream of the SOX2 transcription start site.
source: To further delineate the molecular mechanism of SOX2 regulation by NFATc2, we screened, in silico, the genomic sequences spanning 5 kb up- and downstream of the SOX2 transcription start site (TSS), which identified 4 regions encompassing multiple conserved NFAT binding sequences (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by computational prediction using PWMSCAN for NFAT binding sites.

claim: Alignment with ChIP-seq data of A549 cells showed significant overlap at loci of H3K27Ac occupancy with regions 2 and 3 of SOX2.
source: Alignment with ChIP-seq data of A549 cells retrieved from public databases showed significant overlap at loci of H3K27Ac occupancy with regions 2 and 3, respectively (Figure 6A).
evidence: Demonstrated by genome browser view comparing predicted NFAT sites with H3K27Ac ChIP-seq data from public databases.

claim: Luciferase assays confirmed regions 2 and 3 of SOX2 are active transcriptional regulatory regions.
source: Luciferase assays confirmed these regions are active transcriptional regulatory regions (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase reporter assays showing transcriptional activity of SOX2 regions 1-4.

claim: Transcriptional activities of SOX2 were mediated by sites 1, 2, 4, and 5.
source: Further evaluation with respective SOX2 luciferase reporter revealed transcriptional activities were mediated by sites 1, 2, 4, and 5 (Figure 6B).
evidence: Demonstrated by dual luciferase reporter assays in H441 cells showing activity at these sites.

claim: Using H441 lung cancer cell line with NFATc2 transient overexpression, only sites 1, 4 and 5 showed statistically significant increased reporter activities while those of sites 4 and 5 were reciprocally abolished by CSA treatment.
source: Using H441 lung cancer cell line with NFATc2 transient overexpression, we observed only sites 1, 4 and 5 showed statistically significant increased reporter activities while those of sites 4 and 5 were reciprocally abolished by CSA treatment (Figure 6C).
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase reporter assays with NFATc2 overexpression and CSA treatment.

claim: Site directed mutagenesis of NFAT motifs (GGAAA to GACTA) prevented reporter activities of sites 4 and 5 only.
source: Finally, site directed mutagenesis of NFAT motifs (GGAAA to GACTA) prevented reporter activities of sites 4 and 5 only (Figure 6D), and the findings were supported by data from A549 and H1299 cells ectopically expressing NFATc2, respectively (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase reporter assays with mutant versus wild-type SOX2 reporters in H441, A549, and H1299 cells.

claim: SOX2 sites 4 and 5 are highly conserved across different mammalian species.
source: Notably, sequence homology analysis showed SOX2 sites 4 and 5 are highly conserved across different mammalian species (Figure 6E).
evidence: Demonstrated by sequence alignment showing homologous regions in human, chimpanzee, orangutan, horse, dog, pig, and mouse.

claim: NFATc2 ChIP-qPCR assays using A549 with NFATc2 upregulation showed statistically significant enrichment of sites 4 and 5 sequences compared to vector control.
source: For validation, NFATc2 ChIP-qPCR assays were performed using A549 with NFATc2 upregulation, which showed statistically significant enrichment of sites 4 and 5 sequences compared to vector control (Figure 6F).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR showing enrichment of SOX2 sites 4 and 5 with NFATc2 overexpression.

claim: In HCC827 cells, sites 4 and 5 sequences were significantly enriched by anti-NFATc2 antibody compared to IgG control.
source: In HCC827 cells, sites 4 and 5 sequences were significantly enriched by anti-NFATc2 antibody compared to IgG control. Conversely, these sequences were significantly reduced upon NFATc2 knockout in HCC827, compared to their endogenous levels in control cells, indicating de novo physical binding of NFATc2 to SOX2 at sites 4 and 5 (Figure 6G).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR showing enrichment with anti-NFATc2 antibody versus IgG control, and reduction with NFATc2 knockout.

claim: NFATc2 upregulates SOX2 by binding to its 3' enhancer region at around 3.2 kb (site 4) and 3.6 kb (site 5) from the TSS.
source: Together, the data showed NFATc2 upregulates SOX2 by binding to its 3' enhancer region at around 3.2 kb (site 4) and 3.6 kb (site 5) from the TSS, respectively.
evidence: Concluded from multiple lines of evidence including luciferase assays, mutagenesis, and ChIP-qPCR.

claim: A significant correlation between SOX2 and NFATc2 expressions was observed in 92 moderately to poorly differentiated human lung adenocarcinomas.
source: The clinical significance of NFATc2/SOX2 coupling was further assessed in human lung cancers. To avoid the confounding effect of SOX2 gene amplification in squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), and to focus on tumors with demonstrated involvement of NFATc2, we performed IHC analysis on 92 moderately to poorly differentiated AD. A significant correlation between SOX2 and NFATc2 expressions was observed (Figure 6H).
evidence: Demonstrated by IHC analysis with chi-square test showing Pearson R=0.257, p=0.014.

claim: In lung AD cell lines, NFATc2 and SOX2 transcript expressions were positively correlated.
source: In lung AD cell lines, NFATc2 and SOX2 transcript expressions were also positively correlated (Figure 6I).
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis with Pearson correlation test showing r=0.86, p<0.0001.

claim: Using A549 transduced for NFATc2 overexpression, SOX2 suppression by 2 shSOX2 sequences led to significantly reduced tumorspheres formation.
source: Next, we evaluated whether NFATc2-induced SOX2 upregulation was functionally relevant for its role in sustaining TIC. Using A549 transduced for NFATc2 overexpression, SOX2 suppression by 2 shSOX2 sequences led to significantly reduced tumorspheres formation (Figure 6J–K), and cell motility (Figure 6L).
evidence: Demonstrated by tumorsphere formation assay showing reduction with SOX2 knockdown in NFATc2-overexpressing cells.

claim: SOX2 suppression in NFATc2-overexpressing A549 cells led to reduced cell motility.
source: Next, we evaluated whether NFATc2-induced SOX2 upregulation was functionally relevant for its role in sustaining TIC. Using A549 transduced for NFATc2 overexpression, SOX2 suppression by 2 shSOX2 sequences led to significantly reduced tumorspheres formation (Figure 6J–K), and cell motility (Figure 6L).
evidence: Demonstrated by migration and invasion assays showing reduction with SOX2 knockdown in NFATc2-overexpressing cells.

claim: In vivo, the xenografts enhanced by NFATc2 overexpression were abrogated by SOX2 knockdown.
source: In vivo, the xenografts enhanced by NFATc2 overexpression were also abrogated by SOX2 knockdown (Figure 6M).
evidence: Demonstrated by subcutaneous xenograft experiments showing tumor growth reduction with SOX2 knockdown in NFATc2-overexpressing A549 cells (p<0.0001 by two-way ANOVA).

claim: SOX2 was upregulated in A549 induced for cisplatin resistance (A549 CR) but on NFATc2 knockdown, SOX2 levels were repressed.
source: Similar to NFATc2, SOX2 was also upregulated in A549 induced for cisplatin resistance (A549 CR) but on NFATc2 knockdown, SOX2 levels were repressed (Figure 6N), suggesting NFATc2/SOX2 coupling was functionally active in resistant cancer cells.
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot showing SOX2 upregulation in A549 CR and reduction with NFATc2 knockdown.

claim: While NFATc2 overexpression induced cisplatin resistance of A549 cells, SOX2 silencing restored sensitivity to a level comparable to that of the control cells.
source: Moreover, while NFATc2 overexpression induced cisplatin resistance of A549 cells, SOX2 silencing restored sensitivity to a level comparable to that of the control cells (Figure 6L).
evidence: Demonstrated by MTT assay showing IC50 reduction from 22.0±3µM to 12.7±1.4µM and 11.8±1.15µM with SOX2 knockdown in NFATc2-overexpressing cells.

claim: With NFATc2 knockdown or knockout in HCC827, ALDH+/CD44+-TIC were significantly reduced.
source: We have shown NFATc2 was upregulated in ALDH+/CD44+-TIC, suggesting NFATc2 might regulate this TIC population (Figure 2B). With NFATc2 knockdown or knockout in HCC827, ALDH+/CD44+-TIC were significantly reduced (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: Demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis showing reduction in ALDH+/CD44+ population with NFATc2 knockdown or knockout.

claim: Consistent changes in ALDH+/CD44+-TIC were observed for PDCL#24 with NFATc2 knockdown.
source: Consistent changes were observed for PDCL#24 with NFATc2 knockdown (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis showing reduction in ALDH+/CD44+ population.

claim: Inhibition of calcineurin by CSA and FK506 significantly reduced ALDH+/CD44+-TIC.
source: Further, inhibition of calcineurin by CSA and FK506, respectively, also significantly reduced ALDH+/CD44+-TIC (Figure 7C).
evidence: Demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis showing reduction in ALDH+/CD44+ population with calcineurin inhibitors.

claim: In both A549 with NFATc2 overexpression and in A549 CR cells, ALDH+/CD44+-TIC proportions were increased.
source: Conversely, in both A549 with NFATc2 overexpression and in A549 CR cells, ALDH+/CD44+-TIC proportions were increased (Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis showing increased ALDH+/CD44+ population.

claim: The trend of changes in ALDH+/CD44+-TIC were more consistent with those of the ALDH+ but not CD44+ population, suggesting ALDH might be the main target of NFATc2.
source: Breakdown analysis showed the trend of changes that were more consistent with those of the ALDH+ but not CD44+ population, suggesting ALDH might be the main target of NFATc2.
evidence: Inferred from flow cytometry data showing ALDH+ changes were more consistent than CD44+ changes with NFATc2 manipulation.

claim: Abrogating ALDH1A1 in A549 engineered to overexpress NFATc2 led to significantly suppressed aldefluor activities.
source: ALDH1A1 is the most frequent and important ALDH isozyme reported in lung cancer TIC (Ucar et al., 2009; Tomita et al., 2016). Although ALDH1 is marketed as the major subtype contributing to ALDH activities detected by the ALDEFLUORTM assay, cross-reactivity with other isoforms cannot be excluded. Hence, to explore the part contributed by ALDH1A1, we abrogated ALDH1A1 in A549 engineered to overexpress NFATc2, which led to significantly suppressed aldefluor activities (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis of ALDH activity with ALDH1A1 knockdown, with citations to prior work on ALDH1A1 in lung cancer TIC.

claim: ALDH1A1 expression was suppressed in NFATc2 knockdown or knockout cells, as well as in cells treated with CSA or FK506.
source: ALDH1A1 expression was suppressed in NFATc2 knockdown or knockout cells, as well as in cells treated with CSA or FK506, respectively (Figure 7E–F, Figure 7—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis showing ALDH1A1 mRNA reduction with NFATc2 inhibition.

claim: ALDH1A1 was up-regulated in NFATc2 overexpressing cells and A549 CR cells.
source: Conversely, ALDH1A1 was up-regulated in NFATc2 overexpressing cells and A549 CR cells (Figure 7G–H), indicating NFATc2 regulates ALDH1A1 expression which contributes to the majority of ALDH positivity in ALDH+/CD44+-TIC.
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis showing ALDH1A1 mRNA upregulation with NFATc2 overexpression or cisplatin resistance.

claim: Silencing SOX2 in NFATc2-overexpressing A549 cells consistently prevented the increase of ALDH+ and ALDH+/CD44+ subpopulations only.
source: Further analysis of the role of NFATc2/SOX2 coupling in ALDH1A1 regulation showed silencing SOX2 in NFATc2-overexpressing A549 cells consistently prevented the increase of ALDH+ and ALDH+/CD44+ subpopulations only (Figure 7I).
evidence: Demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis showing prevention of ALDH+ increase with SOX2 knockdown.

claim: The expected upregulation of ALDH1A1 by NFATc2 overexpression was abolished by SOX2 knockdown.
source: Specifically, the expected upregulation of ALDH1A1 was also abolished (Figure 7J).
evidence: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis showing ALDH1A1 mRNA reduction with SOX2 knockdown in NFATc2-overexpressing cells.

claim: Xenografts derived from NFATc2-overexpressing A549 cells showed corresponding upregulation of SOX2 and ALDH1A1.
source: In addition, as analyzed by IHC, xenografts derived from NFATc2-overexpressing A549 cells showed corresponding upregulation of SOX2 and ALDH1A1 (Figure 7K).
evidence: Demonstrated by IHC analysis of xenograft tumors showing coordinated upregulation of NFATc2, SOX2, and ALDH1A1.

claim: Two loci of peak signals encompassing the SOX2 consensus binding motif (ATTCA) were identified in the 5' region of the ALDH1A1 gene at around 27 kb from the TSS (site 1 and 2).
source: To examine the mechanism of SOX2 in ALDH1A1 regulation, ChIP-seq analysis was performed to identify SOX2 binding sequences in PDCL#24 cell line. Two loci of peak signals encompassing the SOX2 consensus binding motif (ATTCA) were identified in the 5' region of the ALDH1A1 gene at around 27 kb from the TSS (site 1 and 2, Figure 7L).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-seq analysis in PDCL#24 cells identifying SOX2 binding sites.

claim: The SOX2 binding loci in ALDH1A1 were located at chr9:75,595,820–75,595,832 and chr9:75,602,860–75,602,872 which overlap with H3K27Ac occupancy and mammalian conserved sequences.
source: Bioinformatics analysis showed these loci were located at chr9:75,595,820–75,595,832 and chr9:75,602,860–75,602,872 which overlap with H3K27Ac occupancy deposited in public ChIP-seq database of A549 cells as well as mammalian conserved sequences (Figure 7L).
evidence: Demonstrated by bioinformatics analysis comparing ChIP-seq peaks with H3K27Ac data and sequence conservation.

claim: No SOX2 binding motif was identified in regions flanking other ALDH isoform genes.
source: On the other hand, no SOX2 binding motif was identified in regions flanking other ALDH isoform genes.
evidence: Stated as a negative finding from computational screening for SOX2 binding sites.

claim: ChIP-q-PCR assay using PDCL#24 cells showed anti-SOX2 antibodies significantly enriched both sequences 1 and 2 of ALDH1A1.
source: To confirm, ChIP-q-PCR assay using PDCL#24 cells was performed which showed anti-SOX2 antibodies significantly enriched both sequences 1 and 2 (Figure 7M).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR showing enrichment of ALDH1A1 sites 1 and 2 with anti-SOX2 antibody versus IgG control.

claim: Luciferase reporter constructs for sites 1 and 2 of ALDH1A1 co-transfected with SOX2 expression plasmids into A549 cells yielded significantly enhanced reporter activities compared to control cells.
source: To study their transcriptional regulatory role, luciferase reporter constructs for sites 1 and 2 were co-transfected with SOX2 expression plasmids into A549 cells which yielded significantly enhanced reporter activities compared to control cells (Figure 7N).
evidence: Demonstrated by dual luciferase reporter assays showing increased activity with SOX2 overexpression.

claim: Compatible results for ALDH1A1 transcriptional regulation were obtained for A549 with NFATc2 overexpression.
source: Compatible results were obtained for A549 with NFATc2 overexpression (Figure 7—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase reporter assays showing increased activity at ALDH1A1 sites 1 and 2 with NFATc2 overexpression.

claim: ALDH1A1 knockdown by siRNA in NFATc2-overexpressing A549 cells led to significant suppression of cell motility.
source: To evaluate whether ALDH1A1 is a functionally relevant target, ALDH1A1 was knocked-down by siRNA in NFATc2-overexpressing A549 cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 3). This led to significant suppression of cell motility (Figure 7O) and cisplatin sensitization (Figure 5N).
evidence: Demonstrated by migration and invasion assays showing reduction with ALDH1A1 knockdown.

claim: ALDH1A1 knockdown in NFATc2-overexpressing A549 cells led to cisplatin sensitization.
source: To evaluate whether ALDH1A1 is a functionally relevant target, ALDH1A1 was knocked-down by siRNA in NFATc2-overexpressing A549 cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 3). This led to significant suppression of cell motility (Figure 7O) and cisplatin sensitization (Figure 5N).
evidence: Demonstrated by MTT assay showing IC50 reduction from 22.8±0.39µM to 12.1±0.93µM and 11.8±0.75µM with ALDH1A1 knockdown.

claim: Moderately to poorly differentiated human lung AD showed statistically significant positive correlation between SOX2 and ALDH1A1 expressions by IHC staining.
source: Furthermore, moderately to poorly differentiated human lung AD showed statistically significant positive correlation between SOX2 and ALDH1A1 expressions by IHC staining (Figure 5O).
evidence: Demonstrated by IHC analysis with chi-square test showing Pearson R=0.23, p=0.028.

claim: In A549 CR cells, intracellular ROS levels were significantly lower compared to parental A549 cells.
source: Alleviation of oxidative stress induced by chemotoxicity promotes cancer cell survival and mediates drug tolerance. Thus, in A549 CR cells, intracellular ROS levels were significantly lower compared to parental A549 cells (Figure 8A).
evidence: Demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis of ROS levels using CellROX Deep Red probe.

claim: NFATc2 silencing by knockdown or knockout led to increased ROS levels.
source: To investigate for possible relation between NFATc2 and ROS modulation, NFATc2 was silenced by knockdown or knockout which led to increased ROS levels (Figure 8B–D).
evidence: Demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis showing increased ROS with NFATc2 knockdown or knockout in HCC827 and PDCL#24 cells.

claim: NFATc2 depletion sensitized PDCL#24 cells to cisplatin treatment, but the addition of the reducing agent NAC reversed cisplatin IC50 to above the control level dose-dependently.
source: As shown in Figure 8E, NFATc2 depletion sensitized PDCL#24 cells to cisplatin treatment, but the addition of the reducing agent NAC reversed cisplatin IC50 to above the control level dose-dependently.
evidence: Demonstrated by MTT assay showing IC50 changes with NFATc2 knockdown and NAC treatment at different doses.

claim: The enhanced resistance of A549 by NFATc2 overexpression was reversed by oxidative stress induced by the glutathione inhibitor BSO.
source: Reciprocally, the enhanced resistance of A549 by NFATc2 overexpression was reversed by oxidative stress induced by the glutathione inhibitor BSO (Figure 8F), consistent with the suggestion that drug resistance by NFATc2 is effected through ROS attenuation.
evidence: Demonstrated by MTT assay showing IC50 reduction from 22.90±1.90µM to 15.78±1.03µM and 13.88±0.66µM with BSO treatment.

claim: Tumorspheres suppression by NFATc2 knockdown was restored by NAC dose-dependently but in control cells, no significant changes were induced even in the presence of additional NAC.
source: Similarly, ROS regulation also supported other tumor phenotypes mediated by NFATc2. For example, tumorspheres suppression by NFATc2 knockdown was restored by NAC dose-dependently but in control cells, no significant changes were induced even in the presence of additional NAC (Figure 8G–H).
evidence: Demonstrated by tumorsphere formation assays with NAC treatment at different doses in HCC827 and PDCL#24 cells.

claim: Cell migration and invasion efficiencies inhibited by NFATc2 depletion were reversed by NAC.
source: Likewise, cell migration and invasion efficiencies inhibited by NFATc2 depletion were reversed by NAC (Figure 6I).
evidence: Demonstrated by transwell migration and invasion assays with NAC treatment in HCC827 cells with NFATc2 knockdown.

claim: Suppression of ROS by NFATc2-overexpression in A549 cells were reversed by silencing SOX2 or ALDH1A1.
source: To further address the involvement of SOX2 coupling and ALDH1A1, we showed suppression of ROS by NFATc2-overexpression in A549 cells were reversed by silencing SOX2 or ALDH1A1, respectively (Figure 8J–K).
evidence: Demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis of ROS levels showing reversal with SOX2 or ALDH1A1 knockdown.

claim: NFATc2/SOX2/ALDH1A1 form a functional axis in the homeostatic regulation of an optimal level of ROS for in vitro tumorigenicity, cell motility, and mediation of drug resistance.
source: Together, the data suggested NFATc2/SOX2/ALDH1A1 form a functional axis in the homeostatic regulation of an optimal level of ROS for in vitro tumorigenicity, cell motility, and mediation of drug resistance.
evidence: Concluded from multiple experiments showing ROS modulation by the NFATc2/SOX2/ALDH1A1 axis affects tumor phenotypes.

claim: Lung cancer results from mutations induced by DNA adducts, free radicals and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated during tobacco smoking and chronic inflammation.
source: Lung cancer results from mutations induced by DNA adducts, free radicals and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated during tobacco smoking and chronic inflammation (Acharya et al., 2010; Okumura et al., 2012; Houghton, 2013).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge with citations to prior literature.

claim: Tumor-initiating cells (TIC) are dynamic cancer cell subsets that display enhanced tumor functions and resilience to treatment.
source: Tumor-initiating cells (TIC) are dynamic cancer cell subsets that display enhanced tumor functions and resilience to treatment but the mechanism of TIC induction or maintenance in lung cancer is not fully understood.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about TIC characteristics.

claim: The mechanism of TIC induction or maintenance in lung cancer is not fully understood.
source: Tumor-initiating cells (TIC) are dynamic cancer cell subsets that display enhanced tumor functions and resilience to treatment but the mechanism of TIC induction or maintenance in lung cancer is not fully understood.
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap motivating the study.

claim: NFATc2 is a novel regulator of lung TIC phenotypes, including tumorspheres, cell motility, tumorigenesis, as well as in vitro and in vivo responses to chemotherapy and targeted therapy.
source: In this study, we show the calcium pathway transcription factor NFATc2 is a novel regulator of lung TIC phenotypes, including tumorspheres, cell motility, tumorigenesis, as well as in vitro and in vivo responses to chemotherapy and targeted therapy.
evidence: Summary statement of the study's main findings.

claim: NFATc2 response elements were identified in the 3' enhancer region of SOX2.
source: Mechanistic investigations identified NFATc2 response elements in the 3' enhancer region of SOX2, and NFATc2/SOX2 coupling upregulates ALDH1A1 by binding to its 5' enhancer.
evidence: Summary statement of mechanistic findings from the study.

claim: NFATc2/SOX2 coupling upregulates ALDH1A1 by binding to its 5' enhancer.
source: Mechanistic investigations identified NFATc2 response elements in the 3' enhancer region of SOX2, and NFATc2/SOX2 coupling upregulates ALDH1A1 by binding to its 5' enhancer.
evidence: Summary statement of mechanistic findings from the study.

claim: Through the NFATc2/SOX2/ALDH1A1 axis, oxidative stress induced by cancer drug treatment is attenuated, leading to increased resistance in a mutation-independent manner.
source: Through this axis, oxidative stress induced by cancer drug treatment is attenuated, leading to increased resistance in a mutation-independent manner.
evidence: Summary statement of the mechanism of drug resistance identified in the study.

claim: Targeting the NFATc2/SOX2/ALDH1A1 axis provides a novel approach for the long-term treatment of lung cancer through TIC elimination.
source: Targeting this axis provides a novel approach for the long-term treatment of lung cancer through TIC elimination.
evidence: Stated as a therapeutic implication of the study's findings.

claim: In some cancers, constitutive activities of inherent embryonic or developmental pathways for stem cell renewal are involved in TIC maintenance, such as the WNT/β-catenin pathway in colonic adenocarcinomas.
source: In some cancers, constitutive activities of inherent embryonic or developmental pathways for stem cell renewal are involved in TIC maintenance, such as the WNT/β-catenin pathway in colonic adenocarcinomas (AD).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about TIC maintenance mechanisms in other cancers.

claim: In tissues with slow cell turnover, mechanisms that elicit cell plasticity and stemness properties during tissue response to intracellular and extracellular stresses are involved in TIC maintenance.
source: In tissues with slow cell turnover, mechanisms that elicit cell plasticity and stemness properties during tissue response to intracellular and extracellular stresses are involved (Valent et al., 2012; Visvader and Lindeman, 2012; Beck and Blanpain, 2013).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge with citations to prior literature.

claim: For the adult lung, stem cell niches or their physiological regulatory mechanisms are ill-defined, and molecular programs sustaining lung TIC are still elusive.
source: For the adult lung, stem cell niches or their physiological regulatory mechanisms are ill-defined, and molecular programs sustaining lung TIC are still elusive.
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: Intracellular free calcium is at the hub of multiple interacting pathways activated by extracellular and/or intrinsic stimulations.
source: Intracellular free calcium is at the hub of multiple interacting pathways activated by extracellular and/or intrinsic stimulations, e.g. EGFR, endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondrial stresses, etc. (Roderick and Cook, 2008; Prevarskaya et al., 2010; Zhao et al., 2013; Déliot and Constantin, 2015), raising the possibility stress signals transduced by calcium pathway mediators could be involved in the induction of TIC phenotypes.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge with citations, leading to a hypothesis.

claim: In cancers of the breast, pancreas, colon and melanoma, the calcium signaling transcription factor nuclear factor of activated T-cells (NFAT) has been shown to contribute to malignant properties including cell invasion, migration, survival, proliferation, stromal modulation and angiogenesis.
source: In cancers of the breast, pancreas, colon and melanoma, the calcium signaling transcription factor nuclear factor of activated T-cells (NFAT) has been shown to contribute to malignant properties including cell invasion, migration, survival, proliferation, stromal modulation and angiogenesis (Werneck et al., 2011; Gerlach et al., 2012; Qin et al., 2014).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge with citations to prior literature.

claim: Information on NFAT's role in TIC phenotypes, especially drug resistance, is limited and details of the molecular pathways linking calcium signaling to TIC induction have not been reported.
source: However, information on its role in TIC phenotypes, especially drug resistance, is limited and details of the molecular pathways linking calcium signaling to TIC induction have not been reported.
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap motivating the study.

claim: NFATc2 induces ALDH+ subsets and ALDH+/CD44+-TIC and enhances drug resistance by ROS scavenging through the NFATc2/SOX2/ALDH1A1 axis.
source: NFATc2 induces ALDH+ subsets and ALDH+/CD44+-TIC and enhances drug resistance by ROS scavenging through the NFATc2/SOX2/ALDH1A1 axis.
evidence: Summary statement of the study's findings on mechanism.

claim: This study reports a novel lung TIC maintenance pathway which links micro-environmental stimulation to induction of stemness phenotypes, evasion of cell death and enhancement of drug resistance.
source: Our study reports a novel lung TIC maintenance pathway which links micro-environmental stimulation to induction of stemness phenotypes, evasion of cell death and enhancement of drug resistance.
evidence: Summary statement of the study's contribution to knowledge.

claim: NFATc2 could be an important target in treatment strategies aiming at disruption of lung TIC.
source: NFATc2 could be an important target in treatment strategies aiming at disruption of lung TIC.
evidence: Stated as a therapeutic implication of the study's findings.

claim: Only one research group has reported NFATc2 expression in 52% of 159 lung cancers and high expression was associated with late tumor stage and poor survival.
source: In the literature, only one research group has reported NFATc2 expression in 52% of 159 lung cancers and similar to our findings, high expression was associated with late tumor stage and poor survival. In their studies, supportive evidences for cell proliferation, invasion and migration were demonstrated by cell models but the in vivo role of NFATc2 and, in particular, its effects on TIC, drug response or mechanisms of action were not addressed (Chen et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2013b).
evidence: Stated as prior literature findings with citations, noting gaps in that work.

claim: SOX2 is an important oncogene for squamous cell carcinomas (SCC) of the lung and other organs through SOX2 locus amplification at 3q26.
source: SOX2 is an important oncogene for squamous cell carcinomas (SCC) of the lung and other organs through SOX2 locus amplification at 3q26 (Hussenet et al., 2010; Lu et al., 2010; Boumahdi et al., 2014).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge with citations to prior literature.

claim: For lung AD, although SOX2 is often expressed at high levels and predicts adverse survivals, distinct genetic mechanisms have not been identified.
source: For lung AD, although SOX2 is often expressed at high levels and predicts adverse survivals (Chou et al., 2013), distinct genetic mechanisms have not been identified, indicating regulatory or signaling aberrations might be involved.
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap with citation, leading to a hypothesis.

claim: In a transgenic mouse model of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with KRAS G12VD mutation and p53 heterozygous inactivation, Singh et al reported NFATc1 acts as a coactivator and transcriptional regulator of SOX2.
source: In a recent study of a transgenic mouse model of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with KRAS G12VD mutation and p53 heterozygous inactivation, Singh et al reported an analogous mechanism involving another NFAT family protein, NFATc1, which acts as a coactivator and transcriptional regulator of SOX2 (Singh et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated as prior literature findings with citation.

claim: NFATc1 played a permissive role for tumor dedifferentiation and expression of epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) genes in pancreatic cancer, while p53 disruption was essential for tumorigenesis.
source: They showed NFATc1 played a permissive role for tumor dedifferentiation and expression of epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) genes, while p53 disruption was essential for tumorigenesis, suggesting under the appropriate genetic context, NFATc1 activation transduces EMT through SOX2 upregulation.
evidence: Stated as prior literature findings with inference about mechanism.

claim: Since chronic inflammation is a known etiology of pancreatic AD, NFATc1 might be a crucial factor involved in the progression of this cancer.
source: The authors proposed since chronic inflammation is a known etiology of pancreatic AD, NFATc1 might be a crucial factor involved in the progression of this cancer.
evidence: Stated as a hypothesis from prior literature.

claim: The ALDH+/CD44+ fraction of lung cancer cells demonstrates the highest tumorigenic capacity compared to counterpart subsets.
source: We have shown the ALDH+/CD44+ fraction of lung cancer cells, despite being the smallest subset, demonstrates the highest tumorigenic capacity compared to counterpart subsets (Liu et al., 2013a).
evidence: Stated as prior finding from the authors' own work with citation.

claim: β-catenin can directly regulate ALDH1A1.
source: Recent reports have shown β-catenin can directly regulate ALDH1A1 (Condello et al., 2015), and since SOX2 can upregulate β-catenin (Yang et al., 2014), this could infer SOX2 might indirectly regulate ALDH1A1 through β-catenin.
evidence: Stated as prior literature findings with citations, leading to a hypothesis.

claim: SOX2 can upregulate β-catenin.
source: Recent reports have shown β-catenin can directly regulate ALDH1A1 (Condello et al., 2015), and since SOX2 can upregulate β-catenin (Yang et al., 2014), this could infer SOX2 might indirectly regulate ALDH1A1 through β-catenin.
evidence: Stated as prior literature findings with citation.

claim: No significant alternation of total or activated β-catenin levels was observed in A549 cells with NFATc2 overexpression and SOX2 knockdown.
source: We thus assessed β-catenin activity by western blot in A549 cells with NFATc2 overexpression and SOX2 knockdown, but no significant alternation of total or activated β-catenin levels was observed in these cells and the possible mechanism of indirect ALDH1A1 upregulation through β-catenin was not supported (Figure 7—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot analysis showing no changes in β-catenin levels.

claim: Current views on cancer stem cells suggest TIC is unlikely to be a single population with unique identifiers; instead, cell plasticity might induce variant TIC populations through dynamic response mechanisms.
source: Current views on cancer stem cells suggest TIC is unlikely to be a single population with unique identifiers; instead, cell plasticity might induce variant TIC populations through dynamic response mechanisms, enabling cancer cells to meet the requirements of a complex micro-environment.
evidence: Stated as current understanding in the field.

claim: Acquired drug resistance is mediated through complex genetic and molecular mechanisms.
source: Acquired drug resistance is mediated through complex genetic and molecular mechanisms (Holohan et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: NFATc2 augments cancer resistance with more prominent effects on tumors treated by cytotoxic chemotherapy.
source: We have shown NFATc2 augments cancer resistance with more prominent effects on tumors treated by cytotoxic chemotherapy.
evidence: Summary statement of the study's findings on drug resistance.

claim: Response to targeted therapy is dominated by addiction to aberrant signaling from the mutant EGFR, and the effects of NFATc2 are modest by comparison.
source: Response to targeted therapy is dominated by addiction to aberrant signaling from the mutant EGFR, and the effects of NFATc2 are modest by comparison.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the study's findings on targeted therapy.

claim: Complementary NFATc2 inhibition might be considered for patients receiving sub-therapeutic treatment regimes of targeted therapy.
source: Nevertheless, as shown by the xenograft model of short term gefitinib treatment, complementary NFATc2 inhibition might be considered for patients receiving sub-therapeutic treatment regimes, e.g., due to the occurrence of serious skin or liver side effects.
evidence: Stated as a therapeutic implication based on the study's findings.

claim: Adaptive antioxidant response to alleviate oxidative stress from ROS surge during systemic therapy is one of the most important mechanisms of drug resistance.
source: Adaptive antioxidant response to alleviate oxidative stress from ROS surge during systemic therapy is one of the most important mechanisms of drug resistance (Zhang et al., 2011), suggested to be accentuated in cancer stem cells (Diehn et al., 2009; Achuthan et al., 2011; Ishimoto et al., 2011; Chang et al., 2014).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge with citations to prior literature.

claim: In adult immortalized bronchial epithelial cells, NFAT can be upregulated in response to inflammatory and carcinogenic stimulation such as benzo-(a)-pyrene and heavy metals.
source: In line with this suggestion, it has been reported in adult immortalized bronchial epithelial cells, NFAT can be upregulated in response to inflammatory and carcinogenic stimulation such as benzo-(a)-pyrene and heavy metals (Huang et al., 2001; Ding et al., 2007; Cai et al., 2011), leading to ROS-induced COX2 pathway signaling and enhanced cell survival (Ding et al., 2006).
evidence: Stated as prior literature findings with citations.

claim: NFAT upregulation in response to carcinogenic stimulation leads to ROS-induced COX2 pathway signaling and enhanced cell survival.
source: In line with this suggestion, it has been reported in adult immortalized bronchial epithelial cells, NFAT can be upregulated in response to inflammatory and carcinogenic stimulation such as benzo-(a)-pyrene and heavy metals (Huang et al., 2001; Ding et al., 2007; Cai et al., 2011), leading to ROS-induced COX2 pathway signaling and enhanced cell survival (Ding et al., 2006).
evidence: Stated as prior literature findings with citation.

claim: Whether ROS is in turn suppressed by NFATc2 through a negative feedback mechanism has not been reported.
source: However, whether ROS is in turn suppressed by NFATc2 through a negative feedback mechanism has not been reported.
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap in the literature.

claim: NFATc2 facilitates ROS scavenging, and this effect is mediated by ALDH1A1 through SOX2 coupling.
source: Our findings supplement this information and show NFATc2 facilitates ROS scavenging, and further implicates this effect is mediated by ALDH1A1 through SOX2 coupling.
evidence: Summary statement of the study's findings on ROS regulation mechanism.

claim: ALDH1A1 plays a role in drug resistance through repressing ROS level.
source: This is consistent with findings of other studies on the role of ALDH1A1 in drug resistance through repressing ROS level (Singh et al., 2013; Raha et al., 2014; Mizuno et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated as consistent with prior literature findings with citations.

claim: This study employed a candidate-based approach and the involvement of other potential NFATc2 and SOX2 targets in cancer phenotypes is not addressed.
source: This study employed a candidate-based approach and the involvement of other potential NFATc2 and SOX2 targets in cancer phenotypes is not addressed.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of the study.
